target_customer: Small and mid-size SaaS teams that handle customer email in Gmail and use tools like Salesforce, Zendesk, Stripe and MailChimp
problem: Support and sales staff had to switch between many SaaS tools to see who an email sender was. Zenbox showed that customer data from the company's own systems in a Gmail sidebar.
business_model: B2B SaaS per seat (four seats free then 25 dollars per seat, per TechCrunch 2012)
product_category: browser extension for email, SaaS integration

founders.name: Sean Grove
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists later roles (OneGraph, Netlify, OpenAI), which came after Zenbox, so they are not prior employers. Education is not listed.

founders.name: Kev Zettler
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a product engineer and technical author. No education or prior employers listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A cross-browser extension that injects a sidebar into Gmail and pulls live data from dozens of SaaS APIs with per-customer authentication, which is moderate work for two engineers.

defensibility.rationale: Value came from the number of integrations, which can be copied one by one. Gmail DOM changes also threatened the extension. No data or network moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent buying or copying Zenbox. TechCrunch (2012-09) contrasts it with Rapportive, which pulled public social data instead.

market_need_then: No spend or complaint data was found for 2011. TechCrunch (2012-09) reported early customers Stripe, Crittercism and Trigger.io.

branding.domain_note: Used zenboxapp.com (app suffix), not the exact .com. The site returned HTTP 503 when fetched.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand itself. Several unrelated companies and a later Chrome extension also use the name Zenbox, which makes it confusable.

pivots.from: Cloudfuji, a cloud platform and app store for open source web apps
pivots.why: TechCrunch reports the team stopped developing Cloudfuji to focus on Zenbox

outcome_analysis: Zenbox entered YC in Summer 2011 and by September 2012 the team had dropped its Cloudfuji platform to focus on the Gmail sidebar, reporting Stripe among early customers. The YC page lists the company as inactive, but no shutdown notice, acquisition or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factor is assigned.
notes: YC status is Inactive; exit type is unknown because no source describes the end. The 20K seed rests on a single database (CB Insights) and has no date. A second CB Insights page names Blockchain Capital for a different ZenBox and was not used. Competitors left empty: the only dated rival source (Rapportive in TechCrunch, 2012-09) is more than a year after the batch. Zenbox was apparently run under the Bushido/Cloudfuji company; TechCrunch names only Sean Grove.
